title: upgrade: attention kernels -> flashattnv2 + rope/rotary fused ops + KV continuous batching & scheduler tweaks
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: Improve single-request latency and throughput for long-context workloads by upgrading our attention execution path to FlashAttentionV2 variants and adding fused rotary/rope operations. This PR also introduces scheduler-level improvements to better utilize KV-cache-friendly batching and continuous batching heuristics, reducing cold-start KV overhead and improving utilization under mixed-latency workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 variants with specialized code paths for rotary and rope encodings. 2) Implement fused ops for rotary/rope where beneficial (fused rotary + softmax prep), reducing kernel launches and memory traffic. 3) Add a KV-cache-aware continuous batching scheduler that groups requests sharing prefixes and reorders micro-batches to maximize KV reuse. 4) Add runtime feature flags and safe fallbacks to previous kernels for unsupported CUDA/driver combinations. 5) Micro-optimizations for kernel launch parameters, shared-memory tiling, and alignment for fp16 and int8 quantized code paths. Benchmarks (internal, measured on p4d and A100 clusters): - End-to-end throughput improvement: 12-25% for long-context generation (seq_len 4k+), depending on model and batch mix. - Median tail latency reduction (p95): 5-15% on continuous-batching workloads. - KV-cache hit efficiency improved by ~18% under prefix-sharing workloads. Compatibility and fallbacks: The new kernels are gated behind a runtime capability check; on unsupported GPUs or older drivers the runtime falls back to the previous stable path. No API changes. Rollout plan: Canary to 5% of hosted traffic (read-only canary first), then Dedicated canaries on selected pools, then gradual ramp to 50% with metrics-based automatic rollback on regressions. Linear tasks: ENG-4281 (kernel upgrades), ENG-4310 (scheduler + KV continuous batching). Testing: unit tests for kernel dispatch, integration tests in perf-canary harness, regression tests in eval-harness with representative prompts, and CI GPU matrix coverage added. Related: references to past attention work and earlier FlashAttention upgrades (see internal PR history).
